description: Makes a patch readable at a glance: colours every port and cable by what it carries, and adds several aids to working with the rack; one in a patch is enough, and it acts on every module

params.text: Colours every jack by what it carries: audio, control voltage, trigger, volt per octave or MPX, in the colours of the set chosen in the menu; a jack nobody has established is drawn off-white
Colours each cable to match the port it comes from; off by default, because a cable's colour belongs to the patch and is saved with it, where everything else here is only drawn over the rack
Redraws every knob in one style, with an arc on its face and the pointer carried past the rim to show what it is set to, so a rack of modules from a dozen makers can be read at a glance
Moves a pattern along each cable in the direction the signal travels, so which end is the source can be seen without tracing it
Lets a two-finger pinch on the trackpad zoom the rack
Dims everything except the cable under the pointer and the two ports it joins, so one cable can be followed through a crowded patch
Picks a cable up from a jack on a click that does not move, where Rack alone would do nothing; a click that moves lands the cable exactly as a drag does
Draws a ring at each click, for a screen recording where the pointer alone does not show what was pressed
Shows Rack's own tooltips larger, in high contrast and directly below the control rather than beside the pointer, with the text size and colours set in the menu

Sets the zoom so a chosen number of whole rack rows fills the window, a fifth of a row showing above and below, and holds the view there: scrolling, the arrow keys, the scroll bar and a cable dragged past the edge all move a row at a time. The number of rows is in the menu, or Command with the up and down arrows. Zooming does nothing while it is on.

A knob must be clicked before the wheel adjusts it; click again for a tenth of the rate, again for a hundredth. An armed knob shows a green disc, a slider a green bar. This is only available when Rack is set to turn knobs with the mouse wheel; the button is greyed out otherwise.

notes: one in a patch is enough; it acts on every module in the rack
bypassing it switches off everything it does, as though it had been removed, and leaves every button as it was set
the scroll wheel moves a slider the pointer is over; the switch for it is in the right-click menu rather than on the panel
the port colours come from a reading of each maker's own text and panels, so a jack whose meaning nobody has established is drawn off-white rather than guessed at
a traced cable stays lit while controls and ports are used; a click on bare panel or empty rack, or Escape, ends the trace
with Whole rows in the window on, the up and down arrows move the view a row at a time, and Command with them shows one more row or one fewer
menu: Colour and rule sets — which set of port colours and rules is in force: Default, DreamRack, and any set saved to a file, with Custom colours… opening the chooser where a set of your own is made
Restore default rules — puts the built-in rules for which family a port belongs to back in the colours file, keeping the colours
Tooltip readability text size — the size of the enlarged tooltips, 100% to 300% of Rack's own
Tooltip readability colours — white on black, or the classic light yellow with black lettering
Scroll wheel adjusts sliders — the wheel moves a slider the pointer is over
Whole rows in the window — how many whole rack rows the window shows, one to five, while that button is on
